title: AutoAccord: deterministic cohort golden-replay & multi-metric gates
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Build AutoAccord, an automated validation harness that runs deterministic golden-replay cohorts against candidate FP8/INT8 quantization profiles and emits multi-metric pass/fail gates for CI and runtime rollouts.

Scope: implement a reproducible pipeline that: (1) constructs cohort slices using production-like query distributions, (2) replays golden prompt sets with deterministic RNG and seeding for repeatability, (3) computes a blended metric suite (semantic fidelity, token-level divergence, top-k logit shifts, and task-specific correctness), (4) applies configurable pass/fail rules and adaptive thresholds, and (5) records artifacts and evidence for audits and rollouts.

Why different: Existing harnesses focus on large aggregate golden suites or single-pass checks. AutoAccord targets cohort determinism and adversarial injection so we can detect brittle edge regressions (e.g., prefix-sensitive failure modes) and provide explainable gates for mixed-precision rollouts. It combines stochastic replay determinism with adversarial examples and per-layer sensitivity tags to drive safe automatic rollouts.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Reproducible runs: using the same seed + config yields byte-identical telemetry artifacts (logs, per-query metrics) across runs.
- Multi-metric gate enforcement: profiles fail if any of the following occur vs gold baseline: (a) absolute QA exact-match drop > 2.5% on curated QA cohort, (b) average top-1 logit-distance increase > 0.08, (c) n-gram (3-gram) F1 decrease > 3.0, or (d) perplexity increase > 6%. Thresholds configurable by project.
- Adversarial seeding: harness supports injection of adversarial prompts generated from the adversary corpus and from model-distillation-based perturbations.
- Integration: outputs a JSON run artifact compatible with the release gating service (schema: run_id, profile_id, metrics, evidence_links).
- Dashboarding: run artifacts render on the accuracy dashboard with per-cohort breakdowns and historical drift lines.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data orchestration: build cohort selector that samples by time-window, user intent tag, token length bucket, and tail-frequency buckets. Implement deterministic hashing + seed composition to ensure stable cohort membership across runs.
2) Replay engine: extend replay service to accept deterministic seed and to optionally replay KV cache warmups according to real session traces to surface caching-affecting regressions.
3) Metric library: implement multi-metric collector: logits-based metrics (L1/L2 of top-k logits), token-level divergence (KL), semantic embedding cosine drift using reference embedder, and task-specific scorers (WER, QA EM).
4) Gate engine: rules DSL to express pass/fail (AND/OR, weighted voting), support for per-cohort and global thresholds, and automatic marking of rollouts for manual review on marginal failures.
5) Evidence & audit: snapshot sample outputs (input + model response + scoring trace), link to PRs and model artifacts, and sign artifacts with run metadata for auditability.
6) CI integration: add a validation job to the quant-merge pipeline that blocks profile promotion on hard failures and surfaces soft failures to the release board.

Trade-offs and design decisions: 
- Deterministic replay vs randomness: deterministic seeding improves reproducibility but may under-expose nondeterministic failure modes. Decision: keep deterministic baseline + an "exploratory stochastic" mode that runs a small number of seeded random trials.
- Metric surface: too many metrics create noise. Decision: expose a blended "primary fidelity" metric plus orthogonal diagnostic metrics in the UI. Primary fidelity is configurable per workload.
- Latency cost vs thoroughness: full KV warmup replay increases runtime cost. Decision: warmup only for cohorts flagged as cache-sensitive and limit warmup length via policy.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Create two alerts: (1) Blocking Failure Alert when any hard gate fails during CI (paged to oncall), (2) Drift Alert when rolling-average primary fidelity drops below threshold over 3 consecutive runs (Slack channel #quant-monitoring).

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal-only, run nightly on a subset (5%) of quant profile candidates for two weeks.
- Beta: enable gating for non-critical profiles and surface soft-failures on the console.
- GA: require passing for production FP8/INT8 profile promotions.

- Design notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/autoaccord_design_v1 (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness/pull/392
- Dashboard draft: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/accuracy/autoaccord (internal)

Open questions: 
- Should the gate thresholds be per-customer as well as global? (PM input needed)
- What is the acceptable cost budget per full run? (Finance/infra question)
- Do we want automated rollback triggers on runtime rollouts or only manual rollbacks?

Next steps: 
- Sprint tasks: implement deterministic seeder (ENG-740112), extend replay engine for KV warmups (ENG-740113), and implement primary fidelity metric (ENG-740114).
- Schedule design review with PM and DS next week (2026-03-17).
